title: POC kickoff: timeline, milestones, access & exec-readout - Synergetic Systems
customer_attendees: Dana Ortiz - Head of Security & Compliance
summary: Kickoff to scope a 6-week POC for deploying an internal assistant over Synergetic's docs. Agreed success criteria (latency, accuracy, cost targets), initial workload estimates, required access (VPC peering + SFTP dataset drop), and a milestone calendar: week 0 kickoff & access, week 2 baseline benchmarks, week 4 midpoint readout, week 6 exec readout. Action items assigned for keys, test data, and benchmark scripts.
action_items: Maya Lin: provide sample dataset (S3 path or SFTP) and token distribution by 2026-04-02
Dana Ortiz: share SOC2 report and encryption/KMS requirements by 2026-04-05
Priya Shah (Redwood SE): send POC runbook + benchmark harness and suggested default configs by 2026-04-01
Alex Martinez (Redwood AE): propose commercial pilot pricing and Dedicated capacity options by 2026-04-06
next_steps: Redwood to share POC runbook and benchmark scripts
Customer to grant VPC peering and temporary service account for data access
Schedule week-2 baseline benchmark call (calendar invite)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Ben (Redwood CSM), Ravi (CTO), Maya (ML Infra), Dana (Head Security), Samir (PM)

[00:00] Alex: Hey team, thanks for carving out time today. Quick intro — I'm Alex, I'm the AE on this account, Priya is our SE who will run the benchmarks and lead the technical onboarding, Ben is CSM for ongoing ops. Can you go around quick on your side?

[00:18] Ravi: Yeah hi, Ravi here. We're trying to validate Redwood for an internal assistant that will route/internal docs, compliance wikis, and some customer support summarization. Priority is to keep everything on-prem or in our VPC for now due to IP and some regulated data.

[00:35] Maya: Maya, ML infra. We're responsible for the infra side. Key constraints: we expect bursts up to ~100 RPS for short windows, baseline 10-15 RPS. Latency target is sub-150ms p99 if possible. We also want to understand token cost per 1M tokens and what tradeoffs look like with quantization or batching.

[00:55] Dana: Dana, security. SOC2 compliance is a must, encryption at rest and in transit, KMS integration, and audit logs. We'll need an architecture diagram and details on access controls for the POC. Also need to know what data leaves our network, if any.

[01:12] Samir: Samir, product. Success criteria for us are: 1) retrieval + answer latency under 500ms for the typical 600-token exchange, 2) >85% acceptable answer rate on our eval set, 3) cost per session below our internal threshold — we'll share a target. Timeline is tight; we want an exec readout in ~6 weeks.

[01:38] Alex: Great, that's helpful. Priya, do you want to walk through the POC plan we usually run and how we map to those success criteria?

[01:46] Priya: Sure. For this engagement we recommend a 6-week POC broken into four milestones: week 0 access and kickoff, week 2 baseline benchmarks (latency, throughput, quality on a seed eval), week 4 midpoint deep dive and tuning, week 6 exec readout with a run-rate cost and ops checklist. Baseline we'll run two workload profiles: interactive chat (lower tokens but tighter latency) and batch summarization (higher tokens, throughput focused).

[02:12] Maya: Can you be specific about what you mean by baseline benchmarks? I'm worried about unrealistic synthetic loads.

[02:20] Priya: Yes — we ask for a sample of your real traffic distribution and a set of 200 eval prompts you care about. We'll run a baseline with your token-length histogram and simulate concurrency matching your 10/100 RPS windows. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and cost estimates for hosted vs Redwood Dedicated vs a private on-prem path. We'll also measure quality scores against your acceptability labels.

[02:52] Ben: We often use continuous batching and KV cache for the retrieval-heavy flows to keep token cost low while preserving latency. For on-prem or VPC deployments we'll talk through prefix caching and whether we can pin KV caches to certain nodes.

[03:06] Ravi: A question — if we go on-prem, do you support air-gapped installs? We have one team that needs no egress.

[03:14] Priya: We do have a private deployment option that can be run in air-gapped environments. For the POC, usually we do a private control-plane with customer-managed networking. For strict air-gap we'd need to arrange for an on-prem package; that adds setup time — usually 2 additional weeks of ops work. We can scope that now if it's a blocker.

[03:37] Dana: That two-week delta is important. Our compliance counsel will not accept anything that has data exfil. Also we need SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS integration. Do you have an HSM integration?

[03:48] Priya: We integrate with cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM via standard KMIP for Private deployments. For the POC, we can run using a customer-managed key if you provide access. We'll attach audit logs to the console and export them to your Splunk/ELK.

[04:05] Samir: On the quality side, we ran an internal eval against a small LLM and got ~78% acceptable. Our exec will want to see an improvement. What are typical gains folks see moving from a baseline open model to a tuned Redwood setup?

[04:18] Priya: It varies, but with retrieval augmentation and small-scale finetune or instruction tuning you often see 5-15 point lift on targeted evals. For the POC we'll test retrieval-augmented pipeline + 1-2 prompt/parameter sweeps. We'll capture ROUGE/F1 where appropriate and a qualitative verdict from your SMEs.

[04:39] Ravi: Cost is another blocker — we need a rule of thumb for 1M tokens. Can you ballpark hosted vs dedicated vs on-prem?

[04:47] Alex: We'll give a pricing note in the follow-up, but high-level: hosted is easiest but highest per-token; Dedicated gives predictability and lower variable cost at higher commit levels; private/on-prem is CAPEX and ops heavy but reduces per-token charges and keeps data local. We'll send concrete numbers once we size the workload.

[05:05] Maya: About sizing — our telemetry says average request is 450 tokens, p99 is 2,200 tokens. Daily volume roughly 4.7M tokens across mixed traffic. How would that map to GPU selection and batch config?

[05:18] Priya: With a distribution like that we typically recommend mixed instance sizing: a smaller fleet for low-latency interactive (A100 or H100 equivalent) and a few larger instances for batch ranking/summarization. We'll draft recommended instance types and batch settings in the runbook. If you need sub-150ms p99 for the 450-token median, we likely need to tune batching down and lean on KV cache for retrieval so we don't re-send long contexts. Quantization can help but has small accuracy trade-offs — we'll include profiles.

[05:55] Dana: For the audit trail — will the POC collect audit logs per request? We need to show who accessed what prompt and redaction options.

[06:03] Priya: Yes we can enable request-level audit logs, redaction hooks, and retention policies. We'll share the schema. Note on redaction: for high-sensitivity fields, we recommend doing client-side tokenization and redaction before sending.

[06:20] Samir: Let's talk gating criteria for passing the midpoint. Is it primarily latency + quality or also ops readiness?

[06:27] Priya: Midpoint gate typically includes: 1) Baseline quality delta (e.g., 5-10% improvement or meeting your >85% bar), 2) Performance: p95/p99 latency within negotiated SLOs at target concurrency, 3) Security checklist (peering/auth/KMS validated), 4) Operational runbook: can your team reproduce a standard benchmark? If all green we prepare exec readout artifacts.

[06:52] Ravi: If we miss the p99 by a bit but quality is there, will Redwood propose fallbacks like model variant routing?

[06:58] Priya: Yes. We have smart routing and fallback to cheaper model variants or different instance pools. For strict SLOs we can pin model versions to Dedicated pools or prioritize traffic on lower-latency nodes. There's a tradeoff and we'll surface cost impact in the benchmark report.

[07:15] Maya: Networking — for the POC what exact access do you need? We prefer VPC peering and a temporary service account. No open inbound.

[07:22] Alex: That's standard. We'll request a VPC peering, a minimal IAM/service account with read-only access to the sample dataset, or you can SFTP the drop. We'll give a checklist in the runbook. For on-prem air-gap, the mechanics differ; we'll outline both options.

[07:36] Dana: Also need to know data residency: if logs or metrics go to Redwood hosted console, are they encrypted and can they be disabled?

[07:44] Priya: Telemetry can be configured; for Private deployments telemetry can be routed to your telemetry stack, and for Hosted we can redact and limit retention. We'll include configuration knobs.

[07:59] Samir: Ok calendar: can we lock in the week-2 baseline call now?

[08:03] Alex: Sure. How about two weeks from now — 2026-04-13 for baseline benchmark review? That aligns with your exec readout on 2026-05-11 (six weeks).

[08:12] Ravi: Works for me.

[08:14] Maya: Works. We'll aim to provide sample data by 2026-04-02 so you have time to run the harness.

[08:20] Priya: Great. I'll send the runbook and the benchmark harness repo link. We'll ask for the token-length histogram and 200 eval prompts. We'll also include a synthetic load recipe so you can reproduce.

[08:32] Ben: From my side I'll collate the CSM checklist and ensure escalation path for Dedicated or Private onboarding.

[08:38] Dana: Final question — any known limitations with retrieval connectors? We use a custom document store (internal vector DB).

[08:45] Priya: We support standard vector formats and connectors; for custom stores we can either host a connector shim or run a local adaptor during POC. We'll add that to the action items to determine integration path.

[08:58] Alex: Wrapping up, I'll summarize next steps and owners.

[09:02] Alex: Recap: Maya to provide dataset + telemetry by 2026-04-02; Dana to share SOC2 and KMS/HSM constraints by 2026-04-05; Priya to send runbook + benchmark harness by 2026-04-01; Alex to deliver pricing and Dedicated options by 2026-04-06. Baseline review call 2026-04-13; midpoint readout week of 2026-04-27; exec readout 2026-05-11.

[09:29] Samir: Sounds good. One small thing — can we get a short slide with the gating criteria for our exec? One page?

[09:35] Ben: Yes we'll produce a one-pager that maps success criteria to metrics and owners.

[09:40] Dana: Thanks everyone. We'll loop in legal if needed for the peering MSA.

[09:44] Alex: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the runbook and calendar invites.

[09:50] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription mis-hears: "K V cash" instead of "KV cache", "Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Redwood Dedicated", jitter in p99/p59 numbers, filler words and overlaps.
